features.name: Academic Attainment
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education the applicant presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic Systems Design
features.description: Captures direct design ownership of agent-based systems, especially bounded autonomy and supporting control infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic Fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as evidenced through concrete engineering improvements.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic evidence is given.
Makes a generic claim about data structures or algorithms.
Gives a specific example of choosing a better structure or redesigning logic algorithmically.
Gives a strong example showing substantial performance, scalability, or tractability improvement from algorithmic skill.

features.name: Applied AI Production Experience
features.description: Captures hands-on experience shipping AI or LLM systems in production with attention to reliability, evaluation, hardening, or guardrails.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer Enablement Mindset
features.description: Captures whether security is framed as helping developers through secure defaults, lower friction, empathy, and workflow integration.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence Specificity
features.description: Captures how well the letter substantiates claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, outcomes, or measurable impact.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go Depth
features.description: Captures how central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's production backend experience.

levels.descriptor: Does not provide meaningful evidence of Go use.
Mentions some Go exposure but not as a core language.
Presents Go as a major working language in production.
Presents Go as the principal or dominant language across core services.

features.name: Language Breadth
features.description: Captures the range of programming languages the applicant presents beyond the core required stack.

levels.descriptor: Shows narrow breadth beyond the main language or two.
Shows moderate breadth across several additional languages.
Shows very broad breadth across many additional languages.

features.name: Narrative Quality
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents a memorable, coherent, role-relevant story or thesis rather than a generic list.

levels.descriptor: Reads like a flat checklist or boilerplate summary.
Is competent and coherent, but relies on common stock framing.
Uses a clear hook or organizing idea that makes the letter easier to remember.
Builds a distinctive, persuasive narrative that meaningfully deepens the case for fit.

features.name: Offensive Security Practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-oriented skill building through CTFs or similar offensive exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-Source Stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public codebases through upstream fixes, maintenance, or support for external users.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Personal Project Ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition and seriousness of self-directed engineering work outside formal job responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or simple side project with limited technical stretch.
Describes a substantial side project with nontrivial systems or reliability concerns.
Describes an ambitious systems project that tackles distributed systems, storage, recovery, consensus, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform Leverage Orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production Engineering Experience
features.description: Captures the amount, breadth, and ownership of professional production software work the letter describes across launch, maintenance, and operation.

levels.descriptor: Meets the baseline only, with limited scope or a small number of launched systems described.
Shows a solid early-career record, with several years and some repeated launch or maintenance work.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with multiple launches and clear production breadth.
Presents an extensive record for this role, combining years, repeated launches, and broad responsibility across production systems.

features.name: Python Depth
features.description: Captures how concretely and convincingly the letter shows Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Reliability and Rigor
features.description: Captures emphasis on correctness, maintainability, failure-awareness, and careful operation in security-sensitive systems.

levels.descriptor: Shows little attention to maintainability or resilience.
Uses generic reliability language without much depth.
Shows a clear maintainer or resilience-oriented framing.
Backs a reliability mindset with concrete attention to failure cases, inherited systems, or stewardship.

features.name: Requirement Mapping
features.description: Captures how explicitly the letter ties the applicant's background to the posting's stated requirements and responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: Makes little direct connection to the posting beyond naming the role.
Mentions some relevant qualifications, but the mapping to the posting is mostly implicit.
Clearly addresses several core requirements or responsibilities from the posting.
Systematically maps experience to the posting, with explicit coverage of the main requirements and responsibilities.

features.name: Role Motivation
features.description: Captures how clearly and convincingly the letter explains why this specific role or security mission is the applicant's intended next step.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in the company or job title with little role-specific reasoning.
Shows some relevant interest, but the motivation remains broad or interchangeable.
Clearly ties motivation to security engineering, developer enablement, or backend tooling.
Gives nuanced and convincing motivation tightly tied to this team's charter and responsibilities.

features.name: Security Assessment Practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience assessing systems for security weaknesses and following remediation through.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security Automation Framing
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the role as scaling scarce security expertise through tooling and automation.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security Credential Strength
features.description: Captures the presence and rigor of formal third-party security credentials.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ or equivalent fundamentals.
Mentions a demanding practical credential such as OSCP or equivalent.

features.name: Security Philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful point of view about what good security engineering is for and how it should operate.

levels.descriptor: No real security viewpoint is articulated beyond general interest.
The letter states that security matters, but the philosophy is thin or generic.
The letter presents a clear viewpoint, such as proactive assistance, quiet resilience, or defaults over policy.
The letter offers a nuanced security philosophy that is clearly tied to the applicant's engineering choices and the role's mission.

features.name: Vulnerability Automation
features.description: Captures experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security workflows.

levels.descriptor: No direct vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general interest in automating security work, but no concrete triage example.
Gives a concrete example of building automation for vulnerability intake or report handling.
Shows clear ownership of triage automation and explains how it reduced manual work or improved flow.

features.name: Writing Polish
features.description: Captures the surface professionalism of the prose, including spelling, grammar, proofreading, and copy accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures remaining dimensions that do not clearly belong to a larger recurring construct, such as learning posture or partnership orientation.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.
